content: I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks.

Built a complete bookmark manager called **Stash**.

Features include:

- Add, edit, and delete bookmarks
- Search across titles, domains, notes, and tags
- Favorites and read-later filters
- Collection organization
- Grid and list layouts
- Sorting controls
- Persistent browser storage
- Responsive mobile design
- Polished empty states, menus, and notifications

The production build passes, and the add/search workflow was verified in Chromium without console errors.

Open the app at [http://maker:4000](http://maker:4000).

This looks really nice, and I can see how it'd help me browse and organize links I've already got. But the whole point for me is saving new links, and I can't tell how that part works from this screen — everything shown looks like it was already in there.

Could you walk me through actually adding one? Say I paste in a link I found — does the app pull in the page's title and details on its own, so I don't have to type all that out myself? That "paste a link and it just saves it sensibly" moment is the main thing I care about. I'd like to see that happen before I can say it does what I need.

content:
That “paste and save” flow now works.

Try it at [http://maker:4000](http://maker:4000):

1. Click **Add bookmark**.
2. Paste any public webpage URL.
3. Stash displays **Reading the page…**
4. It automatically fills the title, description, canonical URL, site identity, preview image, and available keywords.
5. Review or adjust the details, then click **Save to Stash**.

I verified the full flow using an MDN article. Its title and 196-character description were fetched and saved successfully.

If a website blocks metadata access, Stash clearly reports that and still lets you save the URL manually.

That's exactly the moment I wanted — I paste a link and it fills in the title and details for me, and I can still save the link even if a site won't share its info. That covers the main thing I was worried about.

content:
The app is ready as a polished, local-first MVP at [http://maker:4000](http://maker:4000).

### What works

- Paste a public URL and automatically retrieve its title, description, canonical URL, preview image, and available keywords.
- Save links even when metadata retrieval is blocked.
- Edit or delete existing bookmarks.
- Favorite links and manage the read-later state.
- Search titles, domains, notes, and tags. `Ctrl/⌘ + K` focuses search.
- Filter by favorites, unread links, or collection.
- Create persistent custom collections.
- Switch between grid and list layouts.
- Sort by recency, title, or favorites.
- Export the complete library as `stash-bookmarks.json`.
- Retain bookmarks and collections between visits using browser storage.
- Use the principal flows on desktop or mobile.

### Validation completed

I exercised live MDN metadata retrieval and saving, favorites, collection creation, exact search, keyboard navigation, list view, JSON export, and the mobile add dialog. The production build passes with no browser-console errors.

### Current boundary

This version stores everything in the current browser. It does not yet include accounts, cloud synchronization, sharing, browser extensions, or cross-device access. Public-page metadata also requires an internet connection, with the manual-save fallback covering blocked pages.

This does what I set out to do — I can paste a link and have it saved with its details filled in, and I can find, organize, favorite, and clean up my bookmarks afterward. Saving and managing links both work, and the read-later and collections bits are a nice touch for the way I'd actually use it. The browser-only storage is fine for me at this stage.

I'm happy with it. Thanks for the work.
